# Check of M0-f-03b: the work-limit coefficients and the F-WORK hit-rate report (lane `check/M0-f-03b`, flow flow-7, stage group 17, the first check F0, 2026-10-28) — verdict FAIL

Lane `check/M0-f-03b` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, in a Claude Code cloud container (Linux x64), on 2026-10-28
from 00:01 to about 03:10 UTC. `tools/machine_profile.py --id` printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz:4cpu:16gib`.
`node --version` printed `v24.12.0`.

The container rebooted at about 01:30, and the seat continued under the CONTINUE RULE. It kept what its own files and
lane lines establish: the 40-mutant table and results, the strace open log, the M0-b-04 probe and the M0-e-06 run at
version 3. It re-ran the gates and the hand recompute, and it re-ran the two probes that the reboot had cut off.

The seat is the independent checker. It is not the item's author (`build/M0-f-03b`, L-0693). It ran no git command and
changed none of the item's files. It never opened a `selfcheck-*` folder. It planned its probes and mutants from the
brief, the twin entry, C-0444, C-0445 and the code, before it read the author's lane lines.

The seat used two mirrors:

* `/home/user/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-f-03b/mirror` holds version 3, applied by the CLI's `--write`.
* `.../mut` holds version 2 and was used for the mutants, the version-2 controls and the table variants. Every variant
  was restored, and the restored file's sha256 `8c5b12b4…` was checked.

The probe scripts are in `.../probe/` and the logs are beside them. The seat's ledger row is **L-0694**.

This is the first check (F0) under RULING J566 (C-0445's closing clause). It judges the build as it stands:

* the fit machinery in `bench/src/worklimits`;
* the readings of C-0444;
* version 3, staged byte-identical as `bench/test/worklimits/fixtures/workLimits.v3.json`;
* the impact probe's record;
* the shipped version 2, left untouched.

The exit bar's rewrite clause reads PENDING-LONG-RUN.

## Verdict: FAIL — two blockers (B-1, B-2); nine minor notes for M4 in `checks/M0-f-03b-notes.md`

### B-1. No test can fail when the entry stops refusing a fitted table that the loader refuses

At `index.ts:191` the entry calls `parseWorkLimitsText(text)` before it writes anything. Mutant **I02** deletes that
line, and all 327 NEAR tests stay green (`Tests 327 passed (327)`).

The case is reachable. `--date` accepts any `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}`. So `--write --date 2026-02-30` builds a table whose 30
spike cells carry the provenance `M0 spike 2026-02-30`, and the loader refuses that form:

* On the real code the entry refuses, exits 1 and writes nothing (probe P1).
* Under I02 it writes that table to `packages/tables/data/workLimits.json` and exits 0. Every later `loadWorkLimits()`
  then throws.

This refusal is part of the interface's stated contract:

* C-0444 (8) says "nothing is written when … the loader refuses the fitted text".
* The header of `index.ts` lists exit 1 for "a fitted table the loader refuses".

The guard also protects a persisted file (N-45 (b)). A surviving targeted mutant on a stated promise is a blocker
(J180). **CONFIRMED** (mutant run, probe P1).

**Required change.** Add a test to `bench/test/worklimits/entry.test.ts`. It runs
`runWorkLimits(['--write', '--date', '2026-02-30'], …)`, or any fitted text the loader refuses, and checks that the run
exits 1 and writes neither the table nor the summary. I02 must then be KILLED.

Refusing an impossible date at the argument (exit 64) is note N-2. It is hardening and does not replace this test.

### B-2. The hit-rate report silently leaves out every stage the spikes ran whose counters carry no block, so its "≤ 1 per 1 000 on the spikes' runs" cannot fail where those runs do cut

**What the code does.** `stageGroups` (fit.ts) makes one row for each (stage, counter) block that a summary carries.
`hitRates` bounds only those rows. A stage that the spike ran, and that charges a counter, gets no row at all when its
summary has no block for it. The report then says `pass`.

**What the summaries carry.** M0-e-06 runs S1, S3, S4, S5 and S6. In the committed summary, each group has 24 S3 batches
and 68 S5 batches. But its work blocks are one fixed stage per counter: `bench/src/site/report.ts:98 – 101` lists
`hydro.cells` S1, `route.nodes` S4, `grower.turns` and `field.cells` S6. The relief-3000 groups' S4 block also has
n = 0. So `summaries/M0-f-03b.json`'s hit-rate rows for M0-e-06 are S1 × 4, S4 × 2 and S6 × 4. There is no S3 row and no
S5 row, and every row is `after 0, afterExact true` ("none can reach the limit"), with `pass: true`.

**What S3 does.** S3's slice charges `route.nodes` too. It applies the law at stage S3 over the lattice's node count
(`packages/layout/src/siting/slice.ts:97`). A route that reaches the limit takes the `work_cut` rung
(`siting/routes.ts:161`).

**What happens at version 3 on the spikes' own runs.** The seat re-ran M0-e-06's committed form (8 seeds × 4 groups at
CITY) at version 3 in `mirror`, and again at version 2 in `mut` as a control on the same tree. The two mirrors differ
only in `workLimits.json`. Both relief-3000 groups (default and coarse) differ:

* Seed 8: S3 is **refused E_INVARIANT**, recorded in the report's `bugs` (`[{"cls":"E_INVARIANT", …, "stage":"S3"}]`),
  and S4 to S6 are not reached. At version 2, S3 commits all three batches.
* Seeds 2, 3 and 7: the output shifts. On seed 2 the districts go from 93 to 69, the strip faces from 23 to 17 and the
  main gates from 7 to 6.

**The bisection.** The version-3 table was run with groups of rows put back to version 2 (`probe/s3seed8.mts`, the S3
batches' work):

| table | seed 8, S3 batches | seed 2, S3 batches |
|---|---|---|
| version 3 | 110, 1139, REFUSED E_INVARIANT | 86, 1099, 5467 |
| version 3, `route.nodes` at version 2 | 110, 1147, 6470 committed (version 2's S3) | 86, 1267, 6678 (version 2's S3) |
| version 3, the four `insert.*` rows and `tx.facesWalked` at version 2 | still refused | — |
| version 3, the three `cut.*` rows at version 2 | still refused | — |
| version 2 | 110, 1147, 6470 committed | 86, 1267, 6678 |

The cause is version 3's `route.nodes` = 0.3852 + 0.3852 × latticeNodes. It was fitted from 5 S4 samples, and S3's own
route searches have no block.

The kernel's `workLimitHits` is 0 in both runs, because `route.nodes` is a layout counter. The summary's `E_WORK_LIMIT`
census therefore cannot see these cuts either (note N-3).

**Why it is a blocker.** The listed test "the hit rate at the coefficients is ≤ 1 per 1 000 batches on the spikes'
runs" measures a subset of the spikes' runs without saying so, so it cannot fail on the stages it leaves out. The
committed `summaries/M0-f-03b.json` (`pass: true`, `worstPerThousand: 1`, "M0-e-06 … exactly 0") is a wrong result on an
honest input (N-45 (a)). C-0444 (7)'s reading, "the quantile blocks being all there is", does not state that the blocks
miss stages that charge the counters.

The tree still ships version 2 (J566), so no shipped output is wrong. But the report and its test are the machinery
that F0 judges, and the f1 re-fit will reuse them. **CONFIRMED** (both runs, the control, the bisection).

**Required change** (detect and refuse, as N-45 prefers for a fix round):

1. The hit-rate report must list every stage that each summary shows ran: M0-e-06's `stages` and `batches` rows, and
   for M0-c-06 the stages its runs drive (S3's slice, S4, S5, S8).
2. For each such stage it must take the counters the stage charges, read from the stages' declarations (`workLimits`
   in `packages/layout/src/pipeline/base.ts`) or from an explicit table under a choices row.
3. A (stage, counter) the stage charges that has no block is **unbounded**. It is never counted as 0. While one exists,
   `pass` is false: the dry run and `--write` exit 1, naming the missing blocks.
4. C-0444 (7) is amended to say so.
5. A test asserts that on the committed summaries M0-e-06's S3 (`route.nodes` and the kernel counters) and S5 rows come
   out unbounded.

The missing blocks themselves belong to the summaries' owners: M0-e-06 records `route.nodes` only at S4, and M0-c-06
records no route or insert counters. They are a finding for the session, for the f1 round's inputs and Q118 (note N-8).

### What holds

* The gates are green.
* The four listed tests are present and green.
* Of the 40 targeted mutants, 38 are KILLED. I02 survives (B-1). T06 is equivalent on every lawful table (note N-1).
* The hand recompute of cut.candidates matches the file's value.
* The fixed row is untouched.
* The run opens exactly the four summaries.
* The version-3 bytes regenerate byte for byte.
* The shipped file is version 2's PIN bytes.

**CONFIRMED.**

The exit bar's clause "workLimits.json rewritten with measured coefficients" is **PENDING-LONG-RUN** by J566 (3). It is
neither a pass nor a fail here. The other clause, "the coefficient report and the F-WORK hit-rate report written", is
met in form: `summaries/M0-f-03b.json` is committed, and `$PLAT_BENCH_OUT/worklimits-report.json` is written on every
run. B-2 is about what the hit-rate report covers.

## 5 Probes beyond the mutants

* **P1: the B-1 guard on the real entry** (`probe/i02.mts`; the io records and never writes):
  * `2026-10-27 code 0 writes ["/nonexistent/table.json","/nonexistent/summary.json"] … version 3, sha256 1b00cfbd…`
  * `2026-02-30 code 1 writes [] last: worklimits: refused — table 'workLimits', row 'cut.candidates', cell 'floor': provenance 'M0 spike 2026-02-30' is outside §17.1 (6)'s forms (and 29 more)`

  `2026-13-01` and `0000-00-00` give the same result. The loader refuses the fitted text for those dates, so line 191 is
  the only thing between that text and the disk.
* **P2: the loader on edge tables** (`probe/loader.mts`). `v3` is LOADED. The dates `2026-02-30` and `2026-13-01` are
  REFUSED. A counting perUnit or floor with calibratable false is LOADED, at v3 and at v2. That is why T06 is equivalent
  only on lawful tables (note N-1).

  equals the summary's.
